items.title: Return address certification form
items.quote: Please complete the enclosed address certification and mail or upload it by January 15, 2027.
items.computation: The letter prints an explicit calendar date ('by January 15, 2027') rather than a period to count. The sender is a private US bank, not a German authority, so the statutory deemed-delivery rules for administrative letters (§§ 122/41 VwVfG, §§ 187-193 BGB counting of periods after a notional delivery day) do not apply here; the date as written governs. 15 January 2027 falls on a Friday, a normal business day in Germany (no Saturday/Sunday/public-holiday shift needed under §193 BGB). Therefore the due date is the date as printed.

warnings: The letter instructs the recipient to mail or upload a personal address-certification form and threatens restricting online account access if it is not returned — before acting, verify this request through the bank's official, independently-looked-up contact channels (not only the phone/email printed on this letter) to rule out phishing, since 'confirm your details or lose access' is a common scam pattern.
The notice about the telephone switchboard being unavailable on 20 January 2027 is purely informational and creates no obligation or deadline for the recipient; it is not included as an item.
No IBAN or payment details are given in this letter, so none could be checked.
